answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonding collateral in escrows and linking equivocation evidence across identities: when k coordinated identities equivocate on the same conflicting commitment, penalties scale as O(k^2), rather than as isolated fixed fines. Detection can also trigger an exponential multiplier in capital loss through asymmetric depreciation, making a swarm costlier to operate than a single identity; the kernel records correlated proofs, while copper and sable escrow classes may differ in recovery terms.
